/home/shobhitg/src/multi-team-support/scripts/pre_start.lua
/home/shobhitg/src/multi-team-support/scripts/records.lua

For each file, find EVERY string that can reach a player's screen, and report it in the structured output. That includes:
- chat/console messages: game.print, player.print, force.print, surface.print
- flying text (player.create_local_flying_text etc.)
- GUI: caption=, tooltip=, text= on LuaGuiElement .add{} or assignments, including strings inside localised-string tables
- commands.add_command name + help text, and every response string those commands print
- custom alerts, message dialogs, set_goal_description, chart/map tag names, anything else display-bound
- data-stage: localised_name/localised_description, prototype names/descriptions, setting prototypes
- error() messages and log() calls (classify as category 'error'/'log', visibility 'log-only' or 'debug' as appropriate)
- strings handed to other mods or external systems (remote interface return values that get displayed, Discord bridge payloads) → category 'external'

Include even tiny strings ("OK", "Cancel", "+", "▶", "×"). For icon/symbol-only strings add hazard 'symbol-only'. Do NOT report: code comments, table keys, event/style/prototype identifier names used only as identifiers, file paths, pattern strings for string.find, storage keys.

Per string, set:
- status: 'localised' if it is already a {"section.key", ...} locale reference, 'partial' if a locale reference is concatenated/mixed with hardcoded English, 'hardcoded' otherwise.
- dynamic: describe exactly how it is assembled if not static — every '..' concatenation, string.format, table.concat, tick-to-time formatting, number formatting, player/team name interpolation. This is critical: concatenated sentences are the main localisation hazard.
- visibility: 'player' (any player sees it), 'admin' (admin-only), 'debug' (behind a debug flag), 'external' (leaves the game: Discord, RCON, files), 'log-only'.
- hazards, any of: 'concat' (sentence built by concatenation), 'plural' (text hardcodes singular/plural like "1 slot"/"slots" or picks between them in Lua), 'sentence-fragments' (reusable fragment strings composed into sentences elsewhere), 'rich-text' (embeds [color=]/[item=]/[font=] tags), 'server-side-string' (built into a plain Lua string before display, so all players would get one language), 'discord-mirror' (also sent to Discord/external where a LocalisedString cannot go), 'symbol-only', 'sorted-by-text' (list sorted by the display string), 'newlines' (embedded \n layout).

files_scanned must list every file you read (repo-relative), even ones with zero strings. In notes, mention anything structurally interesting for the localisation plan (helper functions that build messages, message pipelines, patterns repeated across files).

Your final output is consumed by a script, not a human — return only the structured data.

2	-- Force utilities: team-force queries, quality sync, surface ownership,
3	-- bounce-home logic, and player clock.
4	-- Team lifecycle operations live in scripts/team_slots and are re-exported
5	-- here so all callers keep the same require path.

35	    local n = 0

37	    return n

43	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
44	        if force_utils.is_team_force(force.name) then
45	            pcall(function() force.unlock_quality("uncommon") end)
46	        end
47	    end
48	end

50	-- ─── Foreign Surface Detection ────────────────────────────────────────
51	
52	local function effective_force(player)
53	    local real_fn = spectator.get_effective_force(player)
54	    return game.forces[real_fn]
55	end
56	
57	function force_utils.on_foreign_surface(player)
58	    local surface = player.surface
59	    if not surface then return false end
60	    local my_force = effective_force(player)
61	    if not my_force then return false end
62	    -- Derive from the single ownership resolver instead of re-implementing it.
63	    -- This also covers mts-v1 ephemeral surfaces (surface_owner_overrides), which
64	    -- the old hand-rolled checks missed -- so a player standing on another team's
65	    -- ephemeral (e.g. MDW) surface now bounces. Unowned surfaces (landing-pen,
66	    -- default nauvis, spectator) return nil -> not foreign, as before.
67	    local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
68	    return owner ~= nil and owner ~= my_force.name
69	end
70	
71	-- ─── Home Surface ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
72	
73	function force_utils.get_home_surface(player)
74	    local force = effective_force(player)
75	    if not force then return nil end
76	    return surface_utils.get_home_surface(force, player.index)
77	end

79	-- Land at ORIGIN, nudged to a non-colliding position when the player has a
80	-- character, so a bounce can't wedge them in water/cliffs on an outer-planet
81	-- variant. Falls back to raw ORIGIN for a characterless controller (god/pen).
82	local function safe_origin(surface, player)
83	    if player.character then
84	        return surface.find_non_colliding_position(player.character.name, helpers.ORIGIN, 8, 0.5)
85	            or helpers.ORIGIN
86	    end
87	    return helpers.ORIGIN
88	end

90	function force_utils.bounce_if_foreign(player)
91	    if not player or not player.connected then return end
92	    local ct = player.controller_type
93	    -- Remote view and the map editor let an admin observe another team's surface
94	    -- without physically being there -- don't yank them home.
95	    if ct == defines.controllers.remote or ct == defines.controllers.editor then return end
96	    if not force_utils.on_foreign_surface(player) then return end
97	
98	    local spawned = storage.spawned_players and storage.spawned_players[player.index]
99	    local home    = spawned and force_utils.get_home_surface(player) or nil
100	    if spawned and home then
101	        helpers.diag("bounce_if_foreign: TELEPORT → " .. home.name .. " (home)", player)
102	        player.teleport(safe_origin(home, player), home)
103	    else
104	        -- Unspawned, OR spawned but the home surface is gone (own team disbanded
105	        -- while standing elsewhere): fall back to the pen rather than stranding
106	        -- the player on a rival surface.
107	        local pen = game.surfaces["landing-pen"]
108	        if pen and pen.valid and player.surface.name ~= "landing-pen" then
109	            helpers.diag("bounce_if_foreign: TELEPORT → landing-pen (fallback)", player)
110	            player.teleport(safe_origin(pen, player), pen)
111	        end
112	    end
113	end

118	    storage.player_clock_start = storage.player_clock_start or {}

120	        storage.player_clock_start[player.index] = game.tick
121	        log("[multi-team-support] clock started for " .. player.name .. " at tick " .. game.tick)
122	    end

1	-- scripts/global_milestones.lua
2	-- Server-wide "first ever" celebrations: first rocket launched and first
3	-- landing on each planet. Each flag fires at most once per save, and the
4	-- announcement is broadcast to every player + drawn on every screen via
5	-- pop_text.global_milestone.
6	--
7	-- LuaSurface.planet.name identifies the planet, but each per-team variant
8	-- is its own planet prototype (mts-vulcanus-1, mts-vulcanus-2, ...), so the
9	-- name is normalized back to its canonical base ("vulcanus") via
10	-- space_age.parse_variant. Without this every team's variant counts as a
11	-- distinct planet and the "first landing" celebration fires once per team
12	-- instead of once per save. Modded planets (any prototype registered as a
13	-- planet) are detected automatically and normalized the same way.
14	
15	local helpers     = require("scripts.helpers")
16	local force_utils = require("scripts.force_utils")
17	local pop_text    = require("scripts.pop_text")
18	local space_age   = require("scripts.space_age")
19	local remote_api  = require("scripts.remote_api")
20	
21	local M = {}
22	
23	function M.init_storage()
24	    storage.global_records = storage.global_records or {}
25	    storage.global_records.first_rocket          = storage.global_records.first_rocket or false
26	    storage.global_records.first_planet_landings = storage.global_records.first_planet_landings or {}
27	    -- force name -> the last announced launch MARK. Seeded from each force's
28	    -- current total on FIRST creation so adding/updating the mod on a live save
29	    -- doesn't re-announce the current neighbourhood -- it stays quiet until the
30	    -- next genuine mark is crossed. (Existing deployments already hold raw totals
31	    -- here from older versions, which give the same quiet behaviour, so the guard
32	    -- leaves them untouched.)
33	    if not storage.rocket_announced then
34	        storage.rocket_announced = {}
35	        for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
36	            if force.valid and (force.rockets_launched or 0) > 0 then
37	                storage.rocket_announced[force.name] = force.rockets_launched
38	            end
39	        end
40	    end
41	end
42	
43	-- Tried in order; first valid path wins. "achievement_unlocked" is the
44	-- ideal fit but isn't in every base game version, so research_completed
45	-- is the fallback (every Factorio install has it).
46	local SOUND_CANDIDATES = {
47	    "utility/achievement_unlocked",
48	    "utility/research_completed",
49	}
50	
51	local function play_global_sound()
52	    for _, p in pairs(game.players) do
53	        if p.connected then
54	            for _, path in ipairs(SOUND_CANDIDATES) do
55	                local ok = pcall(function() p.play_sound{path = path} end)
56	                if ok then break end
57	            end
58	        end
59	    end
60	end
61	
62	local function announce(text_str)
63	    helpers.broadcast(text_str)
64	    pop_text.global_milestone(text_str)
65	    play_global_sound()
66	end
67	
68	-- ─── First rocket launched ────────────────────────────────────────────
69	
70	-- Late-game teams launch rockets continuously (tens of thousands of launches),
71	-- which would flood the Discord bridge. The announcement cadence WIDENS in tiers
72	-- as the running total grows, so the number of posts per tier stays bounded no
73	-- matter how big the base gets:
74	--
75	--   total ≤ 10     every launch      (10 posts)
76	--   total ≤ 100    one per 5         (18 posts: 15, 20, … 100)
77	--   total ≤ 500    one per 25        (16 posts: 125, 150, … 500)
78	--   total ≤ 1000   one per 50        (10 posts: 550, 600, … 1000)
79	--   total > 1000   one per 100       (terminal cadence, forever)
80	--
81	-- So a 45k-launch megabase posts once every ~100 rockets, not the old every-25.
82	-- Each tier is ~10–18 posts, then a flat 1-per-100 — the feed never speeds up
83	-- again past 1000 launches.
84	local ROCKET_TIERS = {
85	    { upto = 10,        step = 1   },
86	    { upto = 100,       step = 5   },
87	    { upto = 500,       step = 25  },
88	    { upto = 1000,      step = 50  },
89	    { upto = math.huge, step = 100 },
90	}
91	
92	--- The announcement step for a given running total (see ROCKET_TIERS).
93	local function rocket_announce_step(total)
94	    for _, tier in ipairs(ROCKET_TIERS) do
95	        if total <= tier.upto then return tier.step end
96	    end
97	    return 100  -- unreachable: the math.huge tier catches everything; defensive
98	end
99	
100	-- Report the HIGHEST step-multiple the counter has reached that hasn't been
101	-- announced yet, rather than testing `total % step == 0`. Two engine realities:
102	--   • force.rockets_launched skips and duplicates values when several rockets
103	--     resolve close together (live logs show "...30254, 30254, 30256..."), so a
104	--     plain exact-multiple test goes silent when the multiple is skipped and
105	--     double-posts when a duplicate lands on one.
106	--   • the announced number should read cleanly, not as a raw overshoot (…45301).
107	-- floor(total/step)*step is the highest multiple the counter has reached; report
108	-- it whenever it exceeds the last reported mark. The feed never goes silent,
109	-- never double-posts, and every announced number past 10 is a step multiple
110	-- (…45300, 45400) — always ending in 0 or 5. Deriving the mark from the CURRENT
111	-- total (not last+step) also means a fresh install / counter reset on an already-
112	-- huge force jumps straight to the current neighbourhood instead of crawling up
113	-- from a low number. A tier boundary widens the step, so the next mark lands on
114	-- the wider grid (after 100 the next is 125, after 1000 it's 1100).
115	--- @return integer|nil  the mark reached — the highest unannounced step multiple
116	---   past 10, or the raw count at/below 10 — or nil when no new mark is due.
117	local function rocket_announce_mark(last, total)
118	    if total < last then return total end          -- counter reset (force recreated): re-arm on raw count
119	    if total <= 10 then                            -- pre-alignment tier: every launch, raw count
120	        return (total > last) and total or nil
121	    end
122	    local step = rocket_announce_step(total)
123	    local mark = math.floor(total / step) * step   -- highest step multiple the counter has reached
124	    return (mark > last) and mark or nil
125	end

127	function M.on_rocket_launched(event)
128	    M.init_storage()
129	
130	    local rocket = event.rocket
131	    if not (rocket and rocket.valid) then return end
132	    local force = rocket.force
133	
134	    -- Team-specific Discord announcement (suppresses vanilla.rocket_launched),
135	    -- throttled by rocket_announce_mark to keep late-game spam down. The reported
136	    -- total is the round MARK (a step multiple), not the raw counter, so the feed
137	    -- reads on clean numbers.
138	    if force_utils.is_team_force(force.name) then
139	        local mark = rocket_announce_mark(storage.rocket_announced[force.name] or 0, force.rockets_launched)
140	        if mark then
141	            storage.rocket_announced[force.name] = mark
142	            local team = (storage.team_names or {})[force.name] or force.name
143	            remote_api.emit_to_bridge("mts.rocket_launched", {
144	                team         = team,
145	                flight_count = mark,
146	                text         = string.format("%s launched a rocket (total: %d)", team, mark),
147	            })
148	        end
149	    end
150	
151	    -- First-ever rocket global milestone (fires once per save).
152	    if storage.global_records.first_rocket then return end
153	    storage.global_records.first_rocket = true
154	
155	    local team_tag = helpers.team_tag_with_leader(force.name) or "A team"
156	    announce(team_tag .. " launched the first rocket into space!")
157	end

161	--- Returns the canonical planet name for a surface, or nil if the surface
162	--- isn't a planet (platform, landing-pen, custom non-planet surface).
163	local function planet_name_of(surface)
164	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return nil end
165	    local planet = surface.planet
166	    if not (planet and planet.valid) then return nil end
167	    -- Collapse per-team variants (mts-vulcanus-1) to their base (vulcanus)
168	    -- so the first-landing gate is shared across every team's copy.
169	    local base = space_age.parse_variant(planet.name)

173	--- Called from the existing on_player_changed_surface handler. `was_spawning`
174	--- is true when the player just transitioned from the landing-pen / spawn
175	--- flow -- in that case we mark the planet as seen silently (so a later
176	--- visit from a platform doesn't fire a misleading "first landing") without
177	--- broadcasting, since the starting planet would otherwise fanfare for the
178	--- very first team to spawn.
179	function M.check_planet_landing(player, was_spawning)
180	    if not (player and player.valid and player.connected) then return end
181	
182	    -- Not actually present: in remote view of someone else's surface.
183	    if player.physical_surface
184	       and player.physical_surface.valid
185	       and player.surface
186	       and player.physical_surface.index ~= player.surface.index then
187	        return
188	    end
189	
190	    -- Spectator force shouldn't trigger first-landing announcements.
191	    if not force_utils.is_team_force(player.force.name) then return end
192	
193	    local pname = planet_name_of(player.surface)
194	    if not pname then return end
195	
196	    M.init_storage()
197	    local landings = storage.global_records.first_planet_landings
198	    if landings[pname] then return end
199	    landings[pname] = player.force.name
200	
201	    if was_spawning then return end
202	
203	    local team_tag   = helpers.team_tag_with_leader(player.force.name)
204	    local planet_tag = "[planet=" .. pname .. "]"
205	
206	    announce(team_tag .. " was first to set foot on " .. planet_tag .. "!")
207	end

39	--- Return a comprehensive state string for a player, including:
40	---   name, force, surface, position, physical_surface, physical_position,
41	---   controller_type, character entity, opened entity (if any), and
42	---   character_inside_entity if the engine reports it. Used by
43	---   diagnostic log statements across the mod.
44	---
45	--- The extra fields beyond controller/position help diagnose
46	--- spectator-related issues:
47	---   • character: nil when the player has no character (god mode,
48	---     spectator force, etc.); a LuaEntity otherwise.
49	---   • opened: the entity whose GUI is currently open (e.g. a space
50	---     platform hub the player is interacting with). Spectator
51	---     transitions can drop this.
52	---   • character_inside_entity: present when the character is "inside"
53	---     a vehicle / hub. Helps pinpoint when MTS-induced state changes
54	---     dismount a player from a hub.
55	function helpers.player_state(player)
56	    if not (player and player.valid) then return "?" end
57	    local ctrl = player.controller_type
58	    local ctrl_name = "?"
59	    for name, id in pairs(defines.controllers) do
60	        if id == ctrl then ctrl_name = name; break end
61	    end
62	    local ps = player.physical_surface
63	    local s  = player.surface
64	
65	    local char = player.character
66	    local char_str = "nil"
67	    if char and char.valid then
68	        char_str = string.format("%s@%s", char.name, fmt_pos(char.position))
69	    end
70	
71	    local opened = player.opened
72	    local opened_str = "nil"
73	    if opened then
74	        -- player.opened can be a LuaEntity, LuaEquipmentGrid, or other
75	        -- types; we only really care about the entity case for
76	        -- spectator diagnostics, but show whatever we get.
77	        if type(opened) == "userdata" and opened.valid and opened.name then
78	            opened_str = opened.name
79	        else
80	            opened_str = tostring(opened)
81	        end
82	    end
83	
84	    -- character_inside_entity may not exist on older Factorio versions;
85	    -- guard it via pcall to avoid crashing the diagnostic itself.
86	    local inside_str = "nil"
87	    pcall(function()
88	        local inside = char and char.valid and char.surface
89	            and char.surface.find_entities_filtered{
90	                position = char.position, radius = 0.1,
91	                invert = true,
92	                name = char.name,
93	            }
94	        if inside and inside[1] then
95	            inside_str = inside[1].name
96	        end
97	    end)
98	
99	    -- LuaControl.hub returns the space platform hub the player is
100	    -- currently sitting in, or nil otherwise. Critical for diagnosing
101	    -- spectator transitions on platforms.
102	    local hub_str = "nil"
103	    local hub = player.hub
104	    if hub and hub.valid then
105	        hub_str = string.format("%s@%s", hub.name, fmt_pos(hub.position))
106	    end
107	
108	    return string.format(
109	        "%s force=%s surface=%s pos=%s phys_surface=%s phys_pos=%s ctrl=%s char=%s opened=%s near=%s hub=%s",
110	        player.name,
111	        player.force and player.force.name or "?",
112	        (s and s.valid) and s.name or "?",
113	        fmt_pos(player.position),
114	        (ps and ps.valid) and ps.name or "?",
115	        fmt_pos(player.physical_position),
116	        ctrl_name,
117	        char_str,
118	        opened_str,
119	        inside_str,
120	        hub_str
121	    )
122	end

152	--- Convert a tick count to a human-readable duration string ("1h 23m 45s").
153	function helpers.fmt_duration(ticks)
154	    local s = math.floor(ticks / 60)
155	    local h = math.floor(s / 3600); s = s % 3600
156	    local m = math.floor(s / 60);   s = s % 60
157	    if h > 0 then return string.format("%dh %02dm %02ds", h, m, s) end
158	    if m > 0 then return string.format("%dm %02ds", m, s) end
159	    return string.format("%ds", s)

162	--- Minute-resolution variant ("1h 23m") for displays refreshed on a slow
163	--- cadence (spawn labels), where a stale seconds digit would look broken.
164	--- Rounds to the NEAREST minute: floor plus refresh staleness read almost
165	--- two minutes behind near a minute boundary, which players notice.
166	function helpers.fmt_duration_coarse(ticks)
167	    local m = math.floor(ticks / 3600 + 0.5)
168	    local h = math.floor(m / 60); m = m % 60
169	    if h > 0 then return string.format("%dh %02dm", h, m) end
170	    return string.format("%dm", m)
171	end

404	--- Display name for a technology, with its level where the engine omits one.
405	---
406	--- The engine builds localised_name in one of two shapes, and only one of
407	--- them needs help:
408	---
409	---   max_level == level   {"", {"technology-name.refined-flammables"}, " 6"}
410	---   max_level >  level   {"technology-name.mining-productivity"}
411	---
412	--- A single-level technology already carries its number, so appending one
413	--- gave "Refined flammables 6 6". Only a multi-level family -- vanilla's
414	--- mining and research productivity, Land Title Registry's land-grant
415	--- ladder -- arrives as a bare family name, which is why eight land-grant
416	--- tiers all rendered identically.
417	---
418	--- Which number to add depends on what the caller holds, and the two
419	--- callers genuinely want different levels, because MTS records the two
420	--- ends of a multi-level family in two different places:
421	---
422	---   tech_research_ticks[force][name]  overwritten every level -> LAST
423	---   records entries[force]            set on the first call   -> FIRST
424	---
425	--- So given a force's LuaTechnology (the research GUIs, which read the
426	--- tick) the answer is the level that force last COMPLETED -- tech.level is
427	--- the level it would research NEXT, so it overshoots by one until the
428	--- family is finished. Given only a prototype (the awards list, which reads
429	--- the record) the answer is the family's STARTING level, because that is
430	--- the only level whose completion that record describes. Labelling that
431	--- row with the span it covers would claim a tier completion nobody
432	--- recorded.
433	---@param tech LuaTechnology|LuaTechnologyPrototype
434	---@return LocalisedString
435	function helpers.tech_label(tech)
436	    local runtime = tech.object_name == "LuaTechnology"
437	    local proto   = runtime and tech.prototype or tech
438	    if proto.max_level <= proto.level then return tech.localised_name end
439	
440	    local label
441	    if runtime then

4	--
5	-- Orchestrates a full team pause / unpause for the mts-v1 API.
6	--
7	-- A team pause is two layers — no active=false entity sweep (see ADR-0001):
8	--   1. pause/power  — the AIRTIGHT freeze: disable every power SOURCE
9	--      (generators + accumulators) the team owns, in a single tick. With the
10	--      grid dead, powered machines simply idle and resume cleanly, and no
11	--      substation+generator island can keep its area running.
12	--   2. pause/wires  — the VISUAL layer (Space-Age-gated): record + cut
13	--      pole-to-pole wires, staggered reconnect on resume. Cosmetic only.
14	--
15	-- We deliberately do NOT use the legacy active=false entity sweep
16	-- (the retired active=false auto-pause feature): killing power is
17	-- airtight by construction and avoids the mid-operation state bugs active=false
18	-- causes. Known gap: burner-fuelled machines run on loaded fuel, not the grid,
19	-- so they keep ticking until that fuel is spent — accepted for now, flagged in
20	-- pause/power.lua.
21	--
22	-- This module is the single entry point both the mts-v1 remote functions and
23	-- the /mts-pause command path call, so both layers fire in the right order.
24	
25	local power       = require("scripts.pause.power")
26	local wires       = require("scripts.pause.wires")
27	local pause_state = require("scripts.pause.state")
28	
29	local control = {}
30	
31	-- ─── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
32	
33	local function is_team_force(force)
34	    return force and force.valid and force.name:find("^team%-") ~= nil
35	end
36	
37	--- Collect the LuaSurface objects owned by a force. We reuse the same owner
38	--- check the rest of MTS uses (surface_utils.get_owner) by delegating to the
39	--- mts-v1 list_team_surfaces query, which is the design's named enumerator —
40	--- but to avoid a circular require on remote_api we resolve surfaces directly
41	--- from the names the caller passes in.
42	--- @param surface_names string[]
43	--- @return LuaSurface[]
44	local function resolve_surfaces(surface_names)
45	    local out = {}
46	    for _, name in pairs(surface_names or {}) do
47	        local s = game.surfaces[name]
48	        if s and s.valid then out[#out + 1] = s end
49	    end
50	    return out
51	end
52	
53	-- ─── Pause ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
54	
55	--- Pause a whole team. Returns true if a pause was started.
56	--- @param force_name    string
57	--- @param surface_names string[]   surfaces owned by the team (from list_team_surfaces)
58	function control.pause_team(force_name, surface_names)
59	    local force = game.forces[force_name]
60	    if not is_team_force(force) then return false end
61	
62	    local surfaces = resolve_surfaces(surface_names)
63	
64	    -- 1. Airtight power cut FIRST, in this tick, so the supply dies immediately
65	    --    rather than over the amortized sweep's many-tick window.
66	    power.freeze(force, surfaces)
67	
68	    -- 2. Visual wire cut (SA-gated, cosmetic, fully defensive).
69	    wires.cut(force, surfaces)
70	
71	    -- 3. Stamp the marker. The power freeze above is synchronous, so the team
72	    --    is paused as of this tick and is_team_paused reflects it immediately.
73	    pause_state.set_paused(force_name, true)
74	    return true
75	end
76	
77	-- ─── Unpause ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	
79	--- Resume a whole team. Returns true if a resume was started.
80	--- @param force_name string
81	--- @param surface_names string[]
82	--- @param opts table  {mode, duration} reserved for v2 (timed pause / sleep-wake)
83	function control.unpause_team(force_name, surface_names, opts)
84	    local force = game.forces[force_name]
85	    if not is_team_force(force) then return false end
86	
87	    local surfaces = resolve_surfaces(surface_names)
88	
89	    -- 1. Re-enable power sources immediately.
90	    power.thaw(force, surfaces)
91	
92	    -- 2. Kick off the staggered visual wire reconnect (no-op if none recorded).
93	    wires.begin_reconnect(force)
94	
95	    -- 3. Clear the marker; the staggered visual reconnect finishes over the
96	    --    next ticks via control.tick().
97	    pause_state.set_paused(force_name, false)
98	    return true
99	end
100	
101	-- ─── Tick ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
102	
103	--- Drive the staggered wire reconnect. Cheap no-op when nothing is pending.
104	--- Wired from events/ticks.lua on the 10-tick cadence.
105	function control.tick()
106	    wires.tick()
107	end
108	
109	return control

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/pause/power.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- The team pause freeze: disable every power SOURCE the team owns.
6	--
7	-- Why kill sources instead of machines or wires
8	-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────
9	-- Setting active=false on every machine (the retired force_pause approach) is
10	-- buggy mid-operation and the bugs are endless; an unpowered machine instead
11	-- keeps its state and simply idles, so resume is clean by construction. Cutting
12	-- pole-to-pole wires (scripts/pause/wires.lua) is NOT a freeze either: a local
13	-- substation fed by a local generator stays an island and powers its whole
14	-- supply area regardless of which trunk wires were cut. The only airtight
15	-- freeze is to kill the SOURCES themselves, immediately, across every owned
16	-- surface. That is this module's single job.
17	--
18	-- This is event-driven: pause/control.lua calls freeze()/thaw() directly at the
19	-- moment of the pause/resume decision. No tick polling, no dirty flag.
20	--
21	-- ✓ RESOLVED — accumulator charge under active=false
22	-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
23	-- The spike is resolved: active=false does NOT stop an accumulator from
24	-- DISCHARGING its stored charge into the network, so a paused base with charged
25	-- accumulators keeps running off them (reported in-game: a docked base's
26	-- assembler still had power). active=false also doesn't drain the charge (an
27	-- earlier headless spike confirmed it persists). So we now SNAPSHOT each
28	-- accumulator's energy, zero it on freeze (no stored power to discharge), and
29	-- RESTORE it on thaw -- the snapshot+restore the comment used to call for.
30	
31	local power = {}
32	
33	-- Diagnostic logging. Off by default; flip to true to trace what the freeze
34	-- disables (per type) in factorio-current.log ([mts:pause/power:DIAG]).
35	local DIAG = false
36	local function diag(msg)
37	    if DIAG then log("[mts:pause/power:DIAG] " .. msg) end
38	end
39	
40	-- Entity TYPES that GENERATE or STORE electricity. Disabling active on these
41	-- stops the supply at the root. Verified as real Factorio 2.0 entity-type
42	-- strings (used as find_entities_filtered{type=...} filters; the array form is
43	-- grounded in dimension-warp/scripts/misc.lua and IR3 control-terrain.lua).
44	--
45	-- ⚠ KNOWN FREEZE LEAK — burner-fuelled machines.
46	-- A burner-generator with fuel already loaded, and more broadly any burner
47	-- machine (burner mining drill, stone furnace, boiler+steam-engine chain that
48	-- is mid-burn) keeps consuming its currently-loaded fuel item for one more
49	-- "burn" even with active=false in some engine versions, because the fuel
50	-- inventory is independent of the active flag. We disable burner-generator
51	-- here, but a fully airtight burner freeze would also need to clear/snapshot
52	-- the fuel/burner inventories — deliberately out of scope for v1; comment kept
53	-- so the leak is discoverable.
54	local POWER_SOURCE_TYPES = {
55	    "generator",                 -- steam engines / turbines
56	    "burner-generator",          -- direct burner -> power (see leak note above)
57	    "solar-panel",               -- daytime supply
58	    "accumulator",               -- stored charge (see SPIKE below)
59	    "reactor",                   -- nuclear heat source feeding generators
60	    "electric-energy-interface", -- modded/scenario infinite or tuned supplies
61	    "fusion-generator",          -- Space Age fusion (no-op pre-SA; type just won't match)
62	}
63	
64	--- Flip active on every power source the force owns on one surface.
65	--- @param surface LuaSurface
66	--- @param force   LuaForce
67	--- @param active  boolean   desired active state (false to freeze)
68	--- @return integer touched  number of entities whose active state changed
69	local function set_sources_on_surface(surface, force, active, charge_store, type_counts)
70	    if not (surface and surface.valid and force and force.valid) then return 0 end
71	    local touched = 0
72	    -- One filtered query per surface (entity-type array filter) instead of a
73	    -- per-chunk walk: power sources are few relative to belts/inserters, so the
74	    -- whole-surface query is cheap and lets the freeze land in a single tick
75	    -- (the airtight requirement — no amortized window where sources stay live).
76	    local sources = surface.find_entities_filtered{
77	        type  = POWER_SOURCE_TYPES,
78	        force = force,
79	    }
80	    for _, ent in ipairs(sources) do
81	        if ent.valid then
82	            type_counts[ent.type] = (type_counts[ent.type] or 0) + 1
83	            if ent.active ~= active then
84	                ent.active = active
85	                touched = touched + 1
86	            end
87	            -- Accumulators: active=false does NOT stop them discharging stored
88	            -- charge into the network. Zero the buffer on freeze (snapshotting it
89	            -- first) so a frozen base has no stored power to run on, and restore
90	            -- it on thaw -- no charge lost, no power leaked.
91	            if ent.type == "accumulator" and ent.unit_number then
92	                if not active then
93	                    charge_store[ent.unit_number] = ent.energy
94	                    ent.energy = 0
95	                else
96	                    local saved = charge_store[ent.unit_number]
97	                    if saved then
98	                        ent.energy = saved
99	                        charge_store[ent.unit_number] = nil
100	                    end
101	                end
102	            end
103	        end
104	    end
105	    return touched
106	end
107	
108	--- Disable (active=false) every power source the force owns across all the
109	--- given surfaces. Call at pause time.
110	--- @param force    LuaForce
111	--- @param surfaces LuaSurface[]   surfaces owned by the force
112	--- @return integer touched
113	function power.freeze(force, surfaces)
114	    return power.set_active(force, surfaces, false)
115	end
116	
117	--- Re-enable (active=true) every power source. Call at resume time.
118	--- @param force    LuaForce
119	--- @param surfaces LuaSurface[]
120	--- @return integer touched
121	function power.thaw(force, surfaces)
122	    return power.set_active(force, surfaces, true)
123	end
124	
125	--- Shared core for freeze/thaw. Runs in every mode (pre-SA teams have power
126	--- sources too) — this airtight freeze is NOT Space-Age-gated; only the
127	--- cosmetic wire layer is.
128	function power.set_active(force, surfaces, active)
129	    if not (force and force.valid) then return 0 end
130	    -- Per-force snapshots: populated on freeze, drained on thaw.
131	    storage.pause_accumulator_charge = storage.pause_accumulator_charge or {}
132	    storage.pause_solar_mult        = storage.pause_solar_mult        or {}
133	    local charge_store = storage.pause_accumulator_charge[force.name] or {}
134	    local solar_store  = storage.pause_solar_mult[force.name]        or {}
135	    storage.pause_accumulator_charge[force.name] = charge_store
136	    storage.pause_solar_mult[force.name]         = solar_store
137	
138	    local touched = 0
139	    local type_counts = {}
140	    for _, surface in pairs(surfaces or {}) do
141	        touched = touched + set_sources_on_surface(surface, force, active, charge_store, type_counts)
142	        -- Solar: active=false does NOT stop a solar panel generating, and surface
143	        -- darkness maxes ~0.85 (night isn't enough). Zero the SURFACE's solar
144	        -- multiplier on freeze (snapshot first) and restore on thaw -- the only
145	        -- airtight way to stop solar output on a frozen surface.
146	        if surface and surface.valid then
147	            if not active then
148	                solar_store[surface.index] = surface.solar_power_multiplier
149	                surface.solar_power_multiplier = 0
150	            else
151	                local saved = solar_store[surface.index]
152	                if saved then
153	                    surface.solar_power_multiplier = saved
154	                    solar_store[surface.index] = nil
155	                end
156	            end
157	        end
158	    end
159	    -- Thaw restored every snapshot; drop the (now empty) stores.
160	    if active then
161	        storage.pause_accumulator_charge[force.name] = nil
162	        storage.pause_solar_mult[force.name]         = nil
163	    end
164	
165	    if DIAG then
166	        local parts = {}
167	        for t, n in pairs(type_counts) do parts[#parts + 1] = t .. "=" .. n end
168	        diag(string.format("%s force=%s touched=%d sources{%s}",
169	            active and "THAW" or "FREEZE", force.name, touched, table.concat(parts, " ")))
170	    end
171	    return touched
172	end
173	
174	return power

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/pause/wires.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- The VISUAL half of a team pause: record and physically cut the team's
6	-- pole-to-pole copper wires so a paused base reads as "unplugged" at a glance,
7	-- then reconnect them in staggered batches on resume so the lights flicker
8	-- back on instead of snapping.
9	--
10	-- THIS LAYER IS COSMETIC. scripts/pause/power.lua is what actually stops the
11	-- power (by disabling the sources). Cutting trunk wires alone is NOT a freeze —
12	-- a local substation+generator island keeps its supply area powered no matter
13	-- which wires are cut. So this module is gated, defensive, and degrades to a
14	-- no-op on any error without ever affecting the airtight power freeze.
15	--
16	-- Space-Age gate: purely a scoping choice — the visual flourish ships with the
17	-- SA-era pause UX. Pre-SA pauses still get the airtight power freeze; they just
18	-- skip the wire theatre.
19	--
20	-- Storage:
21	--   storage.pause_wire_cuts[force_name] = {
22	--       { a_unit, b_unit },   -- recorded pole<->pole copper connections to restore
23	--       ...
24	--   }
25	--   storage.pause_wire_reconnect[force_name] = {
26	--       pairs    = { {a_unit,b_unit}, ... },  -- remaining to reconnect
27	--       idx      = integer,                   -- cursor for staggered reconnect
28	--   }
29	--
30	-- ── API grounding note ────────────────────────────────────────────────
31	-- get_wire_connector / connector.connect_to / connector.disconnect_from and the
32	-- connector.connections enumeration (-> array of WireConnection{target, origin})
33	-- are now VERIFIED against runtime-api.json (2.0.76) AND empirically (a headless
34	-- repro: wire 3 poles, pause -> connections drop to 0, unpause -> restored).
35	-- Reads stay pcall-wrapped as defence in depth. KEY FIX (was the live bug): a
36	-- connection must be cut/restored with its OWN origin -- disconnect_from(target,
37	-- origin) only removes a connection of the MATCHING origin, so the old hardcoded
38	-- origin=script silently no-op'd on real player/robot wires (they "didn't drop").
39	-- We now read each WireConnection.origin, cut with it, record it, and reconnect
40	-- with it. The airtight power freeze (pause/power) is independent of all this.
41	
42	local space_age     = require("scripts.space_age")
43	local surface_utils = require("scripts.surface_utils")
44	
45	local wires = {}
46	
47	-- How many pole pairs to reconnect per driver tick on resume, so a large base
48	-- powers back up as a visible ripple rather than an instant snap.
49	local RECONNECT_PER_TICK = 20
50	
51	-- Diagnostic logging for the connection-enumeration path. Off by default; flip
52	-- to true to trace the cut/reconnect in factorio-current.log (lines prefixed
53	-- [mts:pause/wires:DIAG]). Kept after the origin-bug fix as a debugging aid.
54	local DIAG = false
55	local function diag(msg)
56	    if DIAG then log("[mts:pause/wires:DIAG] " .. msg) end
57	end
58	
59	-- ─── Storage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
60	
61	function wires.init_storage()
62	    storage.pause_wire_cuts      = storage.pause_wire_cuts      or {}
63	    storage.pause_wire_reconnect = storage.pause_wire_reconnect or {}
64	end
65	
66	-- ─── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
67	
68	--- Find an electric pole by unit_number across the given surfaces. Poles are
69	--- the only entities whose wires we record, so the lookup pool is small.
70	--- Build a unit_number -> pole index across the force's surfaces ONCE per
71	--- reconnect batch, so reconnecting N pairs is O(poles + N) instead of
72	--- O(pairs * poles). unit_numbers are globally unique, so a single flat map is
73	--- safe across surfaces.
74	local function build_pole_index(force)
75	    local index = {}
76	    -- Only the force's OWN surfaces can hold its poles (wires.cut records only
77	    -- from those), so scan them instead of every surface in the game (PF-10).
78	    -- Still rebuilt per reconnect batch on purpose: re-deriving owned surfaces
79	    -- each call drops any retired mid-reconnect, avoiding stale LuaEntity handles.
80	    for _, surface in ipairs(surface_utils.owned_surfaces_by_force(force.name)) do
81	        if surface and surface.valid then
82	            local poles = surface.find_entities_filtered{
83	                type  = "electric-pole",
84	                force = force,
85	            }
86	            for _, p in ipairs(poles) do
87	                if p.valid and p.unit_number then index[p.unit_number] = p end
88	            end
89	        end
90	    end
91	    return index
92	end
93	
94	--- Read the pole_copper connector for an entity, or nil. (true = create the
95	--- connector handle if absent; grounded usage passes true here.)
96	local function copper_connector(entity)
97	    if not (entity and entity.valid) then return nil end
98	    local ok, conn = pcall(function()
99	        return entity.get_wire_connector(defines.wire_connector_id.pole_copper, true)
100	    end)
101	    return ok and conn or nil
102	end
103	
104	--- Resolve the far-end electric-pole and its connector handle for one entry in
105	--- a connector's connection list. ENTIRELY pcall-wrapped because the connection
106	--- record's shape (connection.target -> LuaWireConnector, .owner -> LuaEntity)
107	--- is UNVERIFIED against an existing real usage — a wrong field shape must
108	--- degrade to "skip this connection", never throw. Returns target_connector,
109	--- far_pole or nil, nil.
110	local function resolve_far_pole(connection)
111	    local ok, target_conn, far_pole, origin = pcall(function()
112	        local tc = connection.target
113	        local owner = tc and tc.owner
114	        if owner and owner.valid and owner.type == "electric-pole" then
115	            -- The wire's ORIGIN must be used to disconnect/reconnect it:
116	            -- disconnect_from(target, origin) only removes a connection of the
117	            -- MATCHING origin, so a real player/robot wire is untouched by
118	            -- origin=script (the bug). Defaults to player per the WireConnection
119	            -- concept.
120	            return tc, owner, connection.origin or defines.wire_origin.player
121	        end
122	        return nil, nil, nil
123	    end)
124	    if not ok then return nil, nil, nil end
125	    return target_conn, far_pole, origin
126	end
127	
128	-- ─── Record + Cut (pause) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
129	
130	--- Record every pole<->pole copper connection the force owns, then cut it.
131	--- Returns the number of connections cut. Fully defensive: any failure to read
132	--- the connection list yields zero cuts and leaves the base wired.
133	--- @param force    LuaForce
134	--- @param surfaces LuaSurface[]
135	function wires.cut(force, surfaces)
136	    local sa = space_age.is_active()
137	    diag("CUT begin force=" .. tostring(force and force.name) .. " SA=" .. tostring(sa)
138	        .. " #surfaces=" .. tostring(surfaces and #surfaces or 0))
139	    if not sa then diag("CUT skip: not Space Age"); return 0 end  -- visual layer is SA-gated
140	    if not (force and force.valid) then return 0 end
141	    wires.init_storage()
142	
143	    local recorded = {}
144	    local seen     = {}   -- dedupe a<->b vs b<->a
145	    local cut_count = 0
146	    local total_poles, total_conns, samples = 0, 0, 0
147	
148	    for _, surface in pairs(surfaces or {}) do
149	        if surface and surface.valid then
150	            local poles = surface.find_entities_filtered{
151	                type  = "electric-pole",
152	                force = force,
153	            }
154	            total_poles = total_poles + #poles
155	            diag("surface=" .. surface.name .. " poles=" .. #poles)
156	            for _, pole in ipairs(poles) do
157	                local conn = copper_connector(pole)
158	                local a_unit = pole.valid and pole.unit_number or nil
159	                if conn and a_unit then
160	                    -- UNVERIFIED API: connector.connections enumeration is not
161	                    -- grounded in either repo. pcall-guarded so a wrong shape
162	                    -- degrades to "record nothing", never an error.
163	                    local ok, list = pcall(function() return conn.connections end)
164	                    local rok, rlist = pcall(function() return conn.real_connections end)
165	                    if samples < 10 then
166	                        samples = samples + 1
167	                        diag(string.format("pole#%s conn_ok=%s connections_n=%s real_n=%s",
168	                            tostring(a_unit), tostring(ok),
169	                            (ok and type(list) == "table") and tostring(#list) or ("?(" .. type(list) .. ")"),
170	                            (rok and type(rlist) == "table") and tostring(#rlist) or "?"))
171	                    end
172	                    if ok and type(list) == "table" then
173	                        for _, c in pairs(list) do
174	                            total_conns = total_conns + 1
175	                            local target_conn, far_pole, origin = resolve_far_pole(c)
176	                            local b_unit = far_pole and far_pole.unit_number
177	                            if total_conns <= 10 then
178	                                diag(string.format("  conn#%d target=%s owner_type=%s far_unit=%s origin=%s",
179	                                    total_conns, tostring(target_conn ~= nil),
180	                                    tostring(far_pole and far_pole.type), tostring(b_unit), tostring(origin)))
181	                            end
182	                            if target_conn and b_unit then
183	                                local key = (a_unit < b_unit)
184	                                    and (a_unit .. ":" .. b_unit)
185	                                    or  (b_unit .. ":" .. a_unit)
186	                                if not seen[key] then
187	                                    seen[key] = true
188	                                    -- Record the origin too so reconnect restores
189	                                    -- the SAME wire kind (player/robot/script).
190	                                    recorded[#recorded + 1] = { a_unit, b_unit, origin }
191	                                    -- Cut with the wire's ACTUAL origin (using
192	                                    -- a fixed origin=script silently no-ops on a
193	                                    -- player/robot wire -- the reported bug).
194	                                    local cok, cerr = pcall(function()
195	                                        conn.disconnect_from(target_conn, origin)
196	                                    end)
197	                                    if not cok and cut_count == 0 then diag("disconnect_from ERR: " .. tostring(cerr)) end
198	                                    cut_count = cut_count + 1
199	                                end
200	                            end
201	                        end
202	                    end
203	                elseif samples < 10 then
204	                    samples = samples + 1
205	                    diag("pole#" .. tostring(a_unit) .. " conn=NIL (copper_connector returned nil)")
206	                end
207	            end
208	        end
209	    end
210	
211	    storage.pause_wire_cuts[force.name] = recorded
212	    diag(string.format("CUT done force=%s total_poles=%d total_conns=%d cut=%d recorded=%d",
213	        force.name, total_poles, total_conns, cut_count, #recorded))
214	    if cut_count > 0 then
215	        log("[multi-team-support:pause/wires] cut " .. cut_count
216	            .. " pole connections for " .. force.name)
217	    end
218	    return cut_count
219	end
220	
221	-- ─── Staggered Reconnect (resume) ─────────────────────────────────────
222	
223	--- Begin a staggered reconnect of the wires recorded by cut(). The actual
224	--- reconnects happen in wires.tick(), a few per tick, so power ripples back.
225	--- @param force LuaForce
226	function wires.begin_reconnect(force)
227	    if not (force and force.valid) then return end
228	    wires.init_storage()
229	    local recorded = storage.pause_wire_cuts[force.name]
230	    storage.pause_wire_cuts[force.name] = nil
231	    diag("RECONNECT begin force=" .. force.name .. " recorded_pairs=" .. tostring(recorded and #recorded or 0))
232	    if not recorded or #recorded == 0 then return end
233	    storage.pause_wire_reconnect[force.name] = {
234	        pairs = recorded,
235	        idx   = 1,
236	    }
237	end
238	
239	--- Reconnect a fixed batch of recorded pole pairs for one force. Returns true
240	--- once that force's reconnect is finished so the caller can drop it.
241	local function step_reconnect(force_name, state)
242	    local force = game.forces[force_name]
243	    if not (force and force.valid) then return true end
244	
245	    -- Build the pole index ONCE per tick batch (cheap: poles are few), then
246	    -- reconnect this tick's pairs against it. Rebuilt fresh each tick so it
247	    -- always reflects the live surface set (surfaces could have been retired
248	    -- between cut and resume) and never holds stale LuaEntity handles.
249	    local index = build_pole_index(force)
250	
251	    local done = 0
252	    while done < RECONNECT_PER_TICK and state.idx <= #state.pairs do
253	        local pair   = state.pairs[state.idx]
254	        local pole_a = index[pair[1]]
255	        local pole_b = index[pair[2]]
256	        if pole_a and pole_b then
257	            local ca = copper_connector(pole_a)
258	            local cb = copper_connector(pole_b)
259	            if ca and cb then
260	                -- Reconnect with the SAME origin we recorded at cut time, so the
261	                -- restored wire matches the original (player/robot) and a later
262	                -- pause can cut it again.
263	                pcall(function()
264	                    ca.connect_to(cb, false, pair[3] or defines.wire_origin.player)
265	                end)
266	            end
267	        end
268	        state.idx = state.idx + 1
269	        done = done + 1
270	    end
271	
272	    return state.idx > #state.pairs
273	end
274	
275	--- Tick driver for staggered reconnect. Returns immediately when nothing is
276	--- pending, so it is a cheap no-op outside the brief resume window. Event-like:
277	--- it self-clears each force the instant its reconnect finishes (no lingering
278	--- flag polled forever).
279	function wires.tick()
280	    local pending = storage.pause_wire_reconnect
281	    if not pending or not next(pending) then return end
282	    local finished = {}
283	    for force_name, state in pairs(pending) do
284	        if step_reconnect(force_name, state) then
285	            finished[#finished + 1] = force_name
286	        end
287	    end
288	    for _, name in ipairs(finished) do
289	        pending[name] = nil
290	        log("[multi-team-support:pause/wires] reconnect complete: " .. name)
291	    end
292	end
293	
294	return wires

44	    -- create_team_surface, e.g. MTS Dimension Warp's warp/floor/dock worlds).
45	    -- Kept SEPARATE from the two variant maps above on purpose: planet_map.build()
46	    -- rebuilds those from scratch on every on_configuration_changed, so any
47	    -- ephemeral ownership written there was orphaned on each mod update. This map
48	    -- is never touched by build(). See surface_utils.get_owner / team_surfaces.

51	    -- on_configuration_changed via refresh_discovery_techs() so that
52	    -- adding a planet mod mid-save picks up the new discovery techs

57	-- ─── Build Mappings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
58	
59	--- Build the force↔planet bidirectional maps based on team_pool slots.
60	--- Call on_init (after create_team_pool) and on_configuration_changed.
61	--- Idempotent: rebuilds from scratch each call.
62	---
63	--- Iteration uses space_age.list_base_planets_runtime(), which reads
64	--- game.planets directly. This means:
65	---   • Vanilla planets (nauvis, vulcanus, gleba, fulgora, aquilo)
66	---     are picked up.
67	---   • Modded planets (Lignumis, Maraxsis, Muluna, etc.) registered by
68	---     any mod path — data:extend, PlanetsLib:extend, etc. — are also
69	---     picked up.
70	---   • If a player adds a planet mod to an existing save,
71	---     on_configuration_changed re-runs build() and the new modded
72	---     planet appears in the map automatically.
73	---   • Variants for the new planet have already been created at data
74	---     stage by prototypes/planets.lua (which uses the parallel
75	---     list_base_planets_data() iterator), so the runtime lookup
76	---     always finds them.
77	function planet_map.build()
78	    planet_map.init_storage()
79	    if not space_age.is_active() then return end
80	
81	    local max = max_teams()
82	    storage.map_force_to_planets = {}
83	    storage.map_planet_to_force  = {}
84	
85	    for slot = 1, max do
86	        local force_name = "team-" .. slot
87	        local per_team = {}
88	        for _, base in ipairs(space_age.list_base_planets_runtime()) do
89	            local variant = space_age.variant_name(base, slot)
90	            -- Only include variants that were actually created at data
91	            -- stage. game.planets is the canonical runtime accessor —
92	            -- LuaPrototypes has no `planet` key. (Team Starts uses
93	            -- this same pattern.)
94	            if game.planets and game.planets[variant] then
95	                per_team[base] = variant
96	                storage.map_planet_to_force[variant] = force_name
97	            end
98	        end
99	        storage.map_force_to_planets[force_name] = per_team
100	    end
101	end

103	-- ─── Lookups ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
104	
105	--- Return the variant name for a team + base planet, or nil.
106	---   get_variant("team-1", "nauvis") -> "mts-nauvis-1"
107	function planet_map.get_variant(force_name, base_planet)
108	    local map = (storage.map_force_to_planets or {})[force_name]
109	    return map and map[base_planet] or nil
110	end
111	
112	--- Return the team force name that owns a variant planet, or nil.
113	function planet_map.get_force_by_planet(variant_name)
114	    return (storage.map_planet_to_force or {})[variant_name]
115	end
116	
117	--- Return the team's home planet name (their nauvis variant).
118	function planet_map.get_home_planet(force_name)
119	    return planet_map.get_variant(force_name, "nauvis")
120	end

122	-- ─── Force Setup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
123	
124	--- Hide + lock vanilla base planets for a team force. Safe to call at any
125	--- time — it doesn't touch per-team variant locks, so it can run after
126	--- every surface-creation event without clobbering planet-discovery
127	--- research the team has already completed.
128	---
129	--- Reasons to call this:
130	---   - Space Age lazily creates a base planet's surface when something
131	---     first touches it. We re-hide on on_surface_created so the newly-
132	---     created surface stays invisible to teams.
133	---   - Defensive top-up: base planets should always be locked for teams.
134	function planet_map.hide_base_planets_for(force)
135	    if not is_team_force(force.name) then return end
136	
137	    -- Always hide the default nauvis surface from team forces. Teams have
138	    -- either a cloned surface (base 2.0 / VoidBlock) or a planet variant
139	    -- (Space Age); they never play on the shared default nauvis.
140	    --
141	    -- Note: hiding in Platformer mode used to trigger a Factorio SurfaceList
142	    -- engine quirk that dumped god-mode players onto the landing-pen after
143	    -- escaping a remote view. That's now mitigated by the god_pre_remote
144	    -- save/restore in control.lua's on_player_controller_changed handler,
145	    -- so hiding is safe in all modes.
146	    local default_nauvis = game.surfaces["nauvis"]
147	    if default_nauvis and default_nauvis.valid then
148	        helpers.set_surface_hidden(force, default_nauvis, true)
149	    end
150	
151	    if not space_age.is_active() then return end
152	
153	    -- Lock and hide every base planet currently registered, including
154	    -- modded planets. The iterator returns whatever's in game.planets,
155	    -- so a modded planet added to the save (with a fresh /reload or
156	    -- on_configuration_changed) will be locked alongside the vanilla
157	    -- ones automatically.
158	    --
159	    -- Use game.planets[base].surface rather than game.surfaces[base]
160	    -- because in Space Age planet surfaces are created lazily; the
161	    -- canonical access for a planet's surface goes through LuaPlanet.
162	    -- (This matches Team Starts.)
163	    for _, base in ipairs(space_age.list_base_planets_runtime()) do
164	        pcall(function() force.lock_space_location(base) end)
165	        local planet = game.planets and game.planets[base]
166	        if planet and planet.surface and planet.surface.valid then
167	            helpers.set_surface_hidden(force, planet.surface, true)
168	        end
169	    end
170	end
171	
172	--- Hide base planets for every force.
173	function planet_map.hide_base_planets_for_all()
174	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
175	        planet_map.hide_base_planets_for(force)
176	    end
177	end

179	--- Full reset of a team force's space-location locks:
180	---   - Hide + lock all base planets
181	---   - LOCK all of this team's non-home variants (clean slate — wipes any
182	---     planet-discovery research the previous slot occupant completed)
183	---   - UNLOCK the team's home (nauvis) variant
184	---
185	--- ONLY call this in situations where wiping unlocked variants is the
186	--- intended behavior:
187	---   - on_init / on_configuration_changed (fresh world)
188	---   - Slot recycle (new occupant gets a clean map)
189	---   - on_force_reset / on_technology_effects_reset (engine wiped research)
190	---
191	--- Do NOT call from periodic events (on_surface_created, etc.) — it will
192	--- repeatedly clobber planet-discovery unlocks and make the "space map"
193	--- button vanish every time a space platform is built.
194	function planet_map.apply_force_locks(force)
195	    if not is_team_force(force.name) then return end
196	
197	    planet_map.hide_base_planets_for(force)
198	    if not space_age.is_active() then return end
199	
200	    local home = planet_map.get_home_planet(force.name)
201	
202	    -- Lock every variant owned by this team except home (prevents discovery-tech
203	    -- unlocks from a previous occupant leaking to the new one).
204	    local per_team = (storage.map_force_to_planets or {})[force.name] or {}
205	    for _, variant in pairs(per_team) do
206	        if variant ~= home then
207	            pcall(function() force.lock_space_location(variant) end)
208	        end
209	    end
210	
211	    -- Lock every OTHER team's variants. Without this, nauvis variants inherit
212	    -- the base nauvis "default starting planet, unlocked" state at create time,
213	    -- so every team's hub destination list shows all N nauvis variants from
214	    -- every team. Non-nauvis variants are usually locked-by-default, but lock
215	    -- them here too as defense-in-depth in case the engine ever unlocks one
216	    -- (e.g. a modded discovery effect, or a planet prototype change). Foreign
217	    -- slots count regardless of occupancy — team-12 still gets team-13's
218	    -- variants locked even if slot 13 is empty.
219	    local by_variant = storage.map_planet_to_force or {}
220	    for variant, owner in pairs(by_variant) do
221	        if owner ~= force.name then
222	            pcall(function() force.lock_space_location(variant) end)
223	        end
224	    end
225	
226	    -- Unlock the team's home (nauvis variant)
227	    if home then
228	        pcall(function() force.unlock_space_location(home) end)
229	    end
230	end
231	
232	--- Apply locks for all team forces. Same caveat as apply_force_locks.
233	function planet_map.apply_all_force_locks()
234	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
235	        planet_map.apply_force_locks(force)
236	    end
237	end

239	--- Re-derive a team's planet-discovery unlocks from the techs it has ACTUALLY
240	--- researched, and re-apply them. apply_force_locks() clean-slates every
241	--- non-home variant — correct when research was wiped (fresh world, slot
242	--- recycle), but WRONG after a technology-effects reset or a configuration
243	--- change (e.g. a mod update). Those preserve research yet make the engine
244	--- re-point each discovery tech's unlock at the BASE planet, while the
245	--- redirect that unlocks the team's VARIANT only ever runs on
246	--- on_research_finished. So without this, a team that researched and reached
247	--- (say) Vulcanus loses its variant unlock on the next reset — the planet
248	--- relocks and goes dark — until manually unlocked.
249	---
250	--- Calling this after apply_force_locks restores the variant unlocks from the
251	--- researched discovery techs (re-running the on_research_finished redirect for
252	--- every already-completed one). Safe in every context: if research was wiped,
253	--- no discovery tech is researched and this is a no-op, so it never resurrects
254	--- a previous slot occupant's planets on recycle.
255	function planet_map.reapply_discovery_unlocks(force)
256	    if not space_age.is_active() then return end
257	    if not is_team_force(force.name) then return end
258	    for tech_name, base in pairs(storage.discovery_tech_map or {}) do
259	        local tech = force.technologies[tech_name]
260	        if tech and tech.researched then
261	            local variant = planet_map.get_variant(force.name, base)
262	            if variant then
263	                pcall(function() force.unlock_space_location(variant) end)
264	                pcall(function() force.lock_space_location(base) end)
265	            end
266	        end
267	    end
268	end
269	
270	--- Re-derive discovery unlocks for every team force.
271	function planet_map.reapply_all_discovery_unlocks()
272	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
273	        planet_map.reapply_discovery_unlocks(force)
274	    end
275	end

277	-- ─── Surface Creation ────────────────────────────────────────────────
278	
279	--- Get or create the surface for a planet by name. Returns nil on failure.
280	---
281	--- Synchronously pre-generates a 3-chunk radius around origin before
282	--- returning. This is critical for clone_mirror compatibility: when a
283	--- chunk is generated on a team variant, clone_mirror runs clone_area
284	--- on that chunk, which overwrites destination contents — including
285	--- any character entity present in the destination. If chunk
286	--- generation is deferred (queued via request_to_generate_chunks but
287	--- not forced), the player teleports onto an ungenerated chunk,
288	--- Factorio auto-generates it under their feet, clone_mirror
289	--- destroys their character, and the player drops into god mode.
290	---
291	--- force_generate_chunk_requests blocks until all queued chunks
292	--- generate. By the time we return, clone_mirror has run on every
293	--- chunk in the spawn area; the player teleports onto already-cloned
294	--- terrain and their character survives.
295	---
296	--- Mirrors the same fix in compat/vanilla.lua's setup_player_surface.
297	function planet_map.get_or_create_planet_surface(planet_name)
298	    local planet = game.planets and game.planets[planet_name]
299	    if not (planet and planet.valid) then return nil end
300	    local surface = planet.surface
301	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then
302	        -- create_surface triggers lazy generation of the planet's surface
303	        surface = planet.create_surface()
304	    end
305	    if surface and surface.valid then
306	        surface.request_to_generate_chunks({0, 0}, 3)
307	        surface.force_generate_chunk_requests()
308	    end
309	    return surface
310	end
311	
312	-- ─── Discovery Tech Hook ─────────────────────────────────────────────
313	--
314	-- A "discovery tech" is any technology whose effect list contains an
315	-- `unlock-space-location` modifier. Researching it normally unlocks
316	-- the linked space location (e.g. vulcanus). For team forces we
317	-- redirect that unlock to the team's *variant* of that location so
318	-- discovery research never reveals the shared base planet — only the
319	-- team's private copy.
320	--
321	-- We detect discovery techs by inspecting the technology prototype's
322	-- effects rather than matching on name, because:
323	--   • Vanilla uses "planet-discovery-{vulcanus,gleba,fulgora,aquilo}".
324	--   • Modded planets often follow the same naming convention but not
325	--     always (Lignumis uses "planet-discovery-lignumis", Maraxsis
326	--     might use a different scheme, etc.).
327	--   • Some modpacks rename existing techs.
328	--
329	-- Looking at effects directly is robust against any naming.
330	
331	--- Build the discovery-tech map at runtime by scanning every technology
332	--- for an unlock-space-location effect. Cached in storage and rebuilt
333	--- on configuration changes.
334	---
335	--- Returns: { [tech_name] = base_planet_name, ... }
336	local function build_discovery_techs()
337	    local map = {}
338	    if not (prototypes and prototypes.technology) then return map end
339	    for tech_name, tech in pairs(prototypes.technology) do
340	        for _, effect in pairs(tech.effects or {}) do
341	            if effect.type == "unlock-space-location" then
342	                -- The effect's modifier field changed names across
343	                -- Factorio versions; check both the modern field
344	                -- (`space_location`) and any legacy variants. The
345	                -- pcall covers the case where the field exists but
346	                -- isn't a string we can read.
347	                local location = effect.space_location
348	                if location and game.planets and game.planets[location] then
349	                    map[tech_name] = location
350	                end
351	            end
352	        end
353	    end
354	    return map
355	end
356	
357	--- Refresh the cached discovery-tech map. Call from on_init,
358	--- on_configuration_changed, and any time technology prototypes might
359	--- have changed (mod added/removed).
360	function planet_map.refresh_discovery_techs()
361	    if not space_age.is_active() then
362	        storage.discovery_tech_map = {}
363	        return
364	    end
365	    storage.discovery_tech_map = build_discovery_techs()
366	    log("[multi-team-support:planet_map] discovery techs detected: "
367	        .. (next(storage.discovery_tech_map) and "" or "none"))
368	    for tech_name, base in pairs(storage.discovery_tech_map) do
369	        log("  " .. tech_name .. " -> " .. base)
370	    end
371	end
372	
373	--- If the finished tech is a planet discovery, unlock the team's
374	--- variant and lock the base. Called from tech_records on_research_finished.
375	--- Returns true if handled, false if unrelated.
376	function planet_map.on_research_finished(tech)
377	    if not space_age.is_active() then return false end
378	    local map = storage.discovery_tech_map or {}
379	    local base = map[tech.name]
380	    if not base then return false end
381	    local force = tech.force
382	    if not is_team_force(force.name) then return false end
383	
384	    local variant = planet_map.get_variant(force.name, base)
385	    if variant then
386	        pcall(function() force.unlock_space_location(variant) end)
387	        -- Defensive: re-lock the base in case some other event
388	        -- unlocked it. Without this, discovering the variant would
389	        -- leak access to the shared base planet too.
390	        pcall(function() force.lock_space_location(base) end)
391	    end
392	    return true
393	end
394	
395	-- ─── Logistic Request Rewrite ────────────────────────────────────────
396	--
397	-- The hub's "Import from" planet picker can't be filtered per-force in
398	-- Factorio 2.x: lock_space_location only gates schedule destinations,
399	-- and SpaceLocationPrototype.hidden is a global prototype flag. So
400	-- every team's hub still lists every planet variant (and every base
401	-- planet) in the dropdown. Reactive correction: when a player edits a
402	-- team-owned space-platform request, rewrite the slot's import_from
403	-- to the team's own variant of the same base planet.
404	--
405	-- import_from is only meaningful for space-platform requests. A ground
406	-- logistic chest can still carry the field — it rides along when a
407	-- request section is copied from a hub via blueprint, paste-settings,
408	-- or a shared logistic group — but on a planet surface it's inert
409	-- residue. Rewriting it there does nothing except spam the player
410	-- (and, through logistic-group propagation, once per group member),
411	-- so we gate on the entity being on a space platform before touching it.
412	--
413	-- Event payload (2.0.76):
414	--   entity (LuaEntity), section (LuaLogisticSection), slot_index (uint),
415	--   player_index (uint, optional — nil when scripted).
416	--
417	-- import_from may arrive as a string, a {name = "..."} table, or a
418	-- LuaSpaceLocationPrototype userdata — all three reduce to the name.
419	
420	local function planet_name_to_base(name)
421	    return name:match("^mts%-(.+)%-%d+$") or name
422	end
423	
424	function planet_map.on_logistic_slot_changed(event)
425	    if not space_age.is_active() then return end
426	    local entity = event.entity
427	    if not (entity and entity.valid) then return end
428	    local force = entity.force
429	    if not is_team_force(force.name) then return end
430	
431	    -- Only space-platform requests can ship cargo across planets, so only
432	    -- they can leak to a foreign team. surface.platform is nil on planet
433	    -- surfaces, which skips ground chests carrying inert import_from copied
434	    -- from a hub (blueprint / paste-settings / shared logistic group).
435	    local surface = entity.surface
436	    if not (surface and surface.valid and surface.platform) then return end
437	
438	    local section = event.section
439	    if not (section and section.valid) then return end
440	    if not section.is_manual then return end
441	
442	    local slot = section.get_slot(event.slot_index)
443	    if not slot or not slot.value or not slot.import_from then return end
444	
445	    local current = slot.import_from
446	    if type(current) == "table" or type(current) == "userdata" then
447	        current = current.name
448	    end
